title: Hosting vendor selection for the pilot
contextText: Choosing where the Northwind pilot services will be hosted.

segments.text: Thanks for joining, Theo. For context, we need somewhere to host the services for the Northwind pick-path pilot, and we're deciding this week.
Happy to help. I'm Theo Lindqvist, account manager at Estuary Cloud. I look after most of our consulting partners.
Our shortlist is Estuary's managed Kubernetes or running it ourselves on a small cluster.
I'd rather not run our own cluster for a pilot. JJ's opinion, for what it's worth, is that we'd spend a week on plumbing we don't need.
That was going to be my question for you, JJ. How much effort is managed Kubernetes on Estuary?
A couple of days to set up the pipelines. We've done it before on another client.
And we can give you a dedicated namespace with support included for the length of the pilot.
What about data residency? Northwind is strict about keeping floor data in the EU.
Our Frankfurt region covers that. All data stays in the EU.
Has Frankfurt been stable? I remember some noise about outages.
There were two short outages in Frankfurt last year, both under an hour. Nothing this year.
That's acceptable for a pilot.
Then I think we're agreed. We'll host the pilot on Estuary Cloud managed Kubernetes in the Frankfurt region.
Agreed.
Agreed. I'll start on the pipelines Monday.
Theo, the missing piece is pricing. What's the timeline on a committed-use quote?
I'll send you committed-use pricing by Friday February 13.
Good. Please send it to me and copy Priya.
Will do. And a small thing about me, I'm much better on email than on calls, I'm on the road a lot.
Email it is. JJ, anything else you need from Theo?
Just the namespace and credentials once the contract is signed.
Those usually take a day after signature.
Then the critical path is really the pricing and our own sign-off.
Right. Let's reconvene when the pricing is in. Thanks Theo.

note.body:
# Hosting vendor selection for the pilot

**Date:** February 5
**Attendees:** Alex Rivera (Larkspur Labs), Priya Raman (Larkspur Labs), JJ (Larkspur Labs), Theo Lindqvist (Estuary Cloud)

## Summary

The team chose where to host the services for the Northwind pick-path pilot. The shortlist was Estuary Cloud's managed Kubernetes versus a self-run cluster. Theo Lindqvist, account manager at Estuary Cloud, joined to answer questions.

## Discussion

- JJ argued against running a cluster ourselves for a pilot: a week of plumbing we don't need. Setting up pipelines on Estuary's managed Kubernetes takes a couple of days, and the team has done it before for another client.
- Estuary offers a dedicated namespace with support included for the pilot's duration.
- Northwind requires floor data to stay in the EU; Estuary's Frankfurt region covers that.
- Frankfurt had two short outages last year, both under an hour, and none this year. Priya judged that acceptable for a pilot.

## Decisions

- The pilot will be **hosted on Estuary Cloud managed Kubernetes in the Frankfurt region**.

## Action items

- **Theo Lindqvist** — send committed-use pricing by Friday February 13, to Alex with Priya copied.
- **JJ** — start on the deployment pipelines on Monday.
- Namespace and credentials follow about a day after contract signature.

## Notes

- Theo is much easier to reach by email than on calls; he travels a lot.
- The critical path is now the pricing and Larkspur's own sign-off.
